entries.text: When issuing focus-fire orders across multiple turns, keep the designated priority target the same until it is destroyed or disengages; repeatedly re-picking a new 'closest/priority' target each order cycle fragments damage and delays kills even if you still win on aggregate.

If the enemy fleet splits into separate clusters, split your own force to mirror each cluster (matching or exceeding local ship count) rather than keeping one mass formation chasing a scattered enemy - this preserves numerical superiority in every sub-engagement.

Against a slow/stationary clustered enemy, opening with a synchronized massed torpedo alpha-strike on a single high-value target (focus fire) rapidly attrits their PD and lands multiple penetrations/kills - default to this when enemy is stationary and grouped at long range.

When enemy is decisively outnumbered and proposes a draw after losing most capitals, reject and press the attack - finishing off crippled remnants costs little and secures a clean kill rather than leaving a threat alive.

In symmetric cruiser_torpedo mirror matches, concentrating all fire on the enemy's designated 'center' ship invites the same focus-fire back with no asymmetric advantage; consider splitting target priority or feinting to force enemy PD to divide, rather than mirroring their exact TOT-on-flagship tactic.

When both fleets converge to identical <80km/150km compact PD-wall doctrine and matched throttle, the engagement becomes a pure attrition coin-flip with no positional edge; look for ways to gain range, angle, or timing asymmetry (e.g. earlier launch, wider spread, delayed close) instead of mirroring the enemy's stated formation exactly.

When facing pure-torpedo fleets with overwhelming TOT (20+ rounds every ~30s) and your own PD proves unable to stop penetrations, closing range on a straight vector is a losing bet if you die before arriving — every ship was killed in one salvo (multiple module kills per hit) well before reaching coilgun range across ~4 volleys. Before committing to 'close and brawl', estimate time-to-coilgun-rang...

Directives that only say 'evade aggressively' without specifying maneuver type (jink amplitude, vector diversity, out-of-plane thrust) did not prevent a single torpedo salvo from penetrating in this battle — every wave scored multiple hits. When PD/evasion is clearly failing salvo after salvo, escalate to concrete evasive tactics (random high-g lateral jinks, splitting ships onto divergent vectors...
